name: Arr stack
summary: Request films and TV, and have them found, downloaded and filed into your Jellyfin or Plex library - all connected for you

options.label: Downloads and library folder
options.help: On a share. It gets torrents/ and usenet/ (downloads) and media/ (the library: tv, movies, music, books) - point Jellyfin or Plex at media/. Downloads and library must be together, so that finished downloads are linked into the library rather than copied (no double disk space).

options.label: User name
options.help: For every app's web interface (qBittorrent, Prowlarr, Sonarr, Radarr, Bazarr...). Seerr has its own users: those of your Jellyfin or Plex.

options.label: Password
options.help: For every app's web interface, with the user name above. Changing it here changes it in every app.

options.label: Music (Lidarr)
options.help: Albums by the artists you follow, filed into media/music (for Navidrome, Jellyfin or Plex). About 250MB of memory.

options.label: Books (Bookshelf)
options.help: E-books and audiobooks by the authors you follow, filed into media/books (for Calibre-Web or Audiobookshelf). Bookshelf continues Readarr, with Hardcover's book data. About 250MB of memory.

options.label: Usenet downloads (SABnzbd)
options.help: Downloads from Usenet as well as torrents - it needs a Usenet provider's account (added in SABnzbd afterwards). About 150MB of memory.

options.label: FlareSolverr
options.help: Gets Prowlarr past Cloudflare's "checking your browser" page, which some indexers have: tag those indexers flaresolverr in Prowlarr. It runs a browser: about 500MB of memory.

options.label: Subtitle language
options.help: What Bazarr looks for. More languages, and subtitle sources with accounts, can be added in Bazarr.

options.label: Torrent port
options.help: qBittorrent's incoming connections. Forwarding it on your router (TCP and UDP) helps downloads, but isn't needed.
